'''Sir Martin Hairer''' [[Order of the British Empire|KBE]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 14 November 1975)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=Hairer, Martin | id = U282027 | year = 2016 |author=|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U282027| edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is an Austrian-British<!--Prof Hairer himself has said on the Talk page that he has both Austrian and British citizenship--> mathematician and mathematical physicist working in the field of [[stochastic analysis]], in particular [[stochastic partial differential equation]]s. He is Professor of Mathematics at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and at [[Imperial College London]]. He previously held appointments at the  [[University of Warwick]] and the [[Courant Institute]] of [[New York University]].<ref name=wmi/><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/s002200100424| title = Uniqueness of the Invariant Measure for a Stochastic PDE Driven by Degenerate Noise| journal = Communications in Mathematical Physics| volume = 219| issue = 3| pages = 523| year = 2001| last1 = Eckmann | first1 = J.-P. | last2 = Hairer | first2 = M.| arxiv = nlin/0009028| bibcode = 2001CMaPh.219..523E| s2cid = 5565100}}</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=6602190457}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.4007/annals.2006.164.993| title = Ergodicity of the 2D Navier–Stokes equations with degenerate stochastic forcing| journal = Annals of Mathematics| volume = 164| issue = 3| pages = 993| year = 2006| last1 = Hairer | first1 = M. | last2 = Mattingly | first2 = J. | arxiv = math/0406087| s2cid = 11828895}}</ref> In 2014 he was awarded the [[Fields Medal]],<ref name=imu>{{Cite web |title=IMU-Net 66b : Special issue on IMU Prizes and Medals at ICM 2014 in Seoul|website=International Mathematical Union (IMU) |author=Mireille Chaleyat-Maurel |date=2014|url= https://www.mathunion.org/imu-net/archive/2014/imu-net-066b }}</ref> one of the highest honours a mathematician can achieve.<ref>[http://www.snf.ch/SiteCollectionDocuments/horizonte/Horizonte_gesamt/Horizonte_103_E.pdf Daniel Saraga: ''The equation Tamer''], in: ''Horizons'', [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] No. 103, p.&nbsp;26–7</ref> In 2020 he won the 2021 [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]].<ref name=breakthrough>{{Cite web |title=UK mathematician wins richest prize in academia |last=Sample |first=Ian |work=The Guardian |date=10 September 2020 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/science/2020/sep/10/uk-mathematician-martin-hairer-wins-richest-prize-in-academia-breakthrough}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hairer was born in [[Geneva]], Switzerland.<ref name=whoswho/> He attended the Collège Claparède [[Geneva]] where he received his high school diploma in 1994. He entered a school science competition with sound editing software that was developed into Amadeus,<ref name=Amdeus>{{Cite web |title=Amadeus – Audio waveform editors / sound and voice recorders for macOS X |work=hairersoft.com |access-date=10 September 2020 |url= https://www.hairersoft.com/ }}</ref>
and later continued to maintain the software in addition to his academic work; it continued to be widely used {{As of|2020|lc=y}}.<ref name=breakthrough/> He then attended the [[University of Geneva]], where he obtained his Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematics in July 1998, Master of Science in Physics in October 1998 and PhD in Physics under the supervision of [[Jean-Pierre Eckmann]] in November 2001.<ref name="mathgene"/><ref name=cv/>

==Research and career==
Hairer is active in the field of [[stochastic partial differential equation]]s in particular, and in stochastic analysis and stochastic dynamics in general.<ref name="royal"/>  He has worked on variants of [[Hörmander's condition|Hörmander's theorem]], systematisation of the construction of [[Lyapunov functions]] for stochastic systems, development of a general theory of [[ergodicity]] for non-[[Markov process|Markovian systems]], [[Multiple-scale analysis|multiscale analysis techniques]], [[Asymptotic homogenization|theory of homogenisation]], [[Transition path sampling|theory of path sampling]] and theory of [[rough path]]s<ref name="royal"/> and, in 2014, on his theory of [[regularity structure]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Hairer|first1=Martin|title=A theory of regularity structures|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|date=2014|doi=10.1007/s00222-014-0505-4|volume=198|issue=2|pages=269–504|arxiv=1303.5113|bibcode=2014InMat.198..269H|s2cid=119138901}}</ref>

Under the name HairerSoft, he develops [[Macintosh]] software.<ref name=Amdeus/>

==Personal life==
{{Commons category}}
Hairer holds Austrian and British nationality, and speaks French, German and English; he married fellow mathematician Li Xue-Mei in 2003.<ref name=whoswho/><ref name=spouse>{{cite web|url=http://www.xuemei.org|website=xuemei.org|first=Li|last=Xue-Mei|year=2017|title=Xue-Mei Li: About me}}</ref> His father is [[Ernst Hairer]], a mathematician at the University of Geneva.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolchover |first=Natalie |date=2014-08-12 |title=In Noisy Equations, One Who Heard Music |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/in-noisy-equations-one-who-heard-music-20140812/ |access-date=2025-07-30 |work=[[Quanta Magazine]]}}</ref>
